Heritage sites by state

Heritage sites in Haryana: Rakhigarhi, Hisar and Pinjore

Haryana's heritage runs from Harappan cities such as Rakhigarhi, Banawali and Bhirrana to the early historic mound at Agroha, the Tughlaq palace at Hisar, the fort at Hansi, Sheikh Chilli's tomb at Thanesar, the battlefields of Panipat, the Mughal town of Narnaul and the Pinjore gardens. It has no UNESCO World Heritage Site.

We run programmes at Rakhigarhi, Agroha, Hisar, Hansi, Thanesar and Pinjore for groups on request.

Why Haryana matters for ancient Indian history

The plains of Haryana, watered by the Ghaggar and its tributaries, were one of the densest zones of Harappan settlement. Later, the region lay on the main route between the north-west and the Ganga valley, so it saw armies, traders and pilgrims for over two thousand years. Kurukshetra and Thanesar became a sacred region, Hisar and Hansi guarded the western approach to Delhi, and Panipat saw three battles that changed who ruled northern India.

Because Haryana is next to Delhi, it is also the easiest place for Delhi groups to see a Harappan site, an early historic town and a Sultanate palace in a day or two.

Museums in Haryana

  • Rakhigarhi site museum. Finds and models from the Harappan excavations.
  • Sri Krishna Museum, Kurukshetra. Sculpture, manuscripts and art on Kurukshetra themes.
  • Haryana state archaeology museums. Smaller collections at Hisar and Kurukshetra; check current status before visiting.

Harappan sites: Rakhigarhi and its neighbours

Rakhigarhi, in Hisar district, is among the largest Harappan sites known, with several mounds spread around a living village. Excavations have exposed planned streets, drains, brick houses, a cemetery and evidence of craft work. In 2019, a study of ancient DNA from a woman buried at Rakhigarhi was published, and it has been widely discussed; our ancient DNA and the Harappan debate session explains what it does and does not show. On site, our Rakhigarhi programme walks through the mounds and the village together.

Nearby sites fill out the picture. Bhirrana, in Fatehabad, has early layers that some scholars date to the 5th millennium BCE or earlier, though the dates are debated. Banawali, also in Fatehabad, had a fortified town with a radial street plan. Kunal, Farmana and Mitathal add pre-Harappan and Harappan phases. Groups starting from Delhi can combine a city day with a Rakhigarhi day.

Early historic and Sultanate sites

Agroha, near Hisar, is a large mound linked by tradition with the Agrawal community. Excavations have found remains of a town of the early centuries CE, with coins and a stupa, and our Agroha programme explains how a mound becomes a landscape.

Hisar was founded by Firoz Shah Tughlaq in the 1350s as Hisar-i Firoza. The palace complex has the Gujri Mahal, a mosque, underground chambers and a reused stone pillar of the Mauryan or later period; see our Hisar Firoz Shah palace visit. Hansi, a short drive away, has the Asigarh fort, an old stronghold rebuilt in many periods and linked to the 1857 uprising; our Hansi Asigarh fort visit covers it.

Kurukshetra, Thanesar and the Mughal north

Thanesar (Sthaneshvara) was the capital of Harsha's family in the early 7th century, and the mound of Harsh ka Tila preserves its layers. In the town is the tomb of the Sufi Sheikh Chilli, a Mughal-period tomb with a madrasa, often compared to the Taj Mahal in miniature; see our Sheikh Chilli tomb and Thanesar programme. Brahma Sarovar and the many tirthas of Kurukshetra are living pilgrimage places.

Panipat has the Kabuli Bagh mosque built by Babur after the 1526 battle, and Ibrahim Lodi's tomb. Narnaul, in the south, has the tomb of Ibrahim Khan Sur, the Jal Mahal and Birbal ka Chhatta. Kos minars, Mughal milestones, still stand along the old highway near Palwal and Kurukshetra. Pinjore, near Panchkula, has a terraced Mughal garden of the 17th century, laid out under Fidai Khan; our Pinjore gardens programme reads it as landscape design.

What Haryana's mounds teach about method

Most of Haryana's ancient sites are not standing buildings but mounds (theh or tila) of earth built up from centuries of houses, floors and rubbish. This is what makes them useful for teaching archaeology. A mound shows how settlements grow upward, why archaeologists dig in layers, and why a trench in one corner may not represent the whole town. At Rakhigarhi, houses of the present village sit on top of parts of the ancient city, which raises real questions about who owns and protects a site.

The sites also show how archaeologists build chronologies. Pottery styles, radiocarbon dates and the order of layers are combined to separate early, mature and late Harappan phases. Debates over the very early dates proposed for Bhirrana are a good example of how science and interpretation meet. Our sessions on chronology and archaeological dating, and on heritage and urban development, use Haryana's sites as case studies.

Later sites raise different questions. Hisar's palace reuses an older pillar, Thanesar's mound mixes several periods, and the kos minars along the highway mark a Mughal road system that modern roads still follow. For students, Haryana is a compact place to learn how one region stores many histories at once.

Is there a UNESCO site in Haryana?

No. Haryana has no inscribed World Heritage Site as of October 2026. The Capitol Complex in Chandigarh, part of a serial site of Le Corbusier's work, lies in the Union Territory of Chandigarh, which is a separate administrative unit.

Planning a heritage trip in Haryana

Hisar is the base for Rakhigarhi, Agroha, Hansi and the palace, and makes a good two-day trip from Delhi. Kurukshetra and Thanesar are on the road to Chandigarh, with Pinjore at the end. Winter is best. Check the ASI or state archaeology website before you go. Our programmes can be booked singly or combined into a study tour for your group.

How we run this

  • Schools: a Rakhigarhi visit with a lecture on the first cities.
  • Colleges: a two-day Hisar circuit with Rakhigarhi, Agroha, Hisar and Hansi.
  • Companies and families: a weekend at Pinjore or Thanesar with a specialist.

Everything is arranged on request: dates, length, level and language are agreed with you, and no payment is taken until you approve the plan. Write to us or use the programme finder.

Questions people ask

What are the main archaeological sites in Haryana?

Rakhigarhi, Bhirrana, Banawali, Kunal and Farmana for the Harappan period; Agroha and Harsh ka Tila at Thanesar for the early historic period. Rakhigarhi is the largest and the most widely studied, and has a site museum.

Does Haryana have a UNESCO World Heritage Site?

No. As of October 2026 Haryana has no inscribed World Heritage Site. The nearby Capitol Complex in Chandigarh, part of the serial listing of Le Corbusier's architecture, is in a separate Union Territory, though it serves as Haryana's capital.

Why is Rakhigarhi important?

It is one of the largest Harappan cities, and excavations have revealed streets, houses, crafts and a cemetery. Ancient DNA from one burial, published in 2019, made it central to debates on the population history of South Asia.

Can we visit Rakhigarhi with an archaeologist?

Yes. Talaash Heritage runs a Rakhigarhi programme for schools, colleges and adult groups, and a longer Delhi and Rakhigarhi programme that pairs the site with Delhi's museums. Both are arranged on request for your dates.

What are the historical places near Hisar?

The Firoz Shah palace in Hisar, the Asigarh fort at Hansi, the Agroha mound and Rakhigarhi are all within a short drive, and can be combined into a one or two day trip.
